screens.prompt: In B7, count how many of the five steps have a date in B2:B6.

hints.syntax: Start with = and close the bracket: =COUNTA(B2:B6).
hints.func-counta: The dates sit in a text column, so counting numbers finds none of them; COUNTA counts anything that is not blank.
hints.require-ref: Point COUNTA at B2:B6 rather than pasting the three dates in: the sheet has to stay the source of the answer.
hints.value: That is not how many steps are dated. Three of the five cells in B2:B6 hold a date and two are empty.
hints.error: COUNTA of a range never fails on text; dividing its answer by zero returns #DIV/0!.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
COUNT looks for numbers and the dates are text, so it answers zero
there is nothing to add up, and adding is not counting
a count divided by zero returns #DIV/0!
the dates typed into the formula, so the count stops following the sheet
the range stops before Publish and Archive, so two dated steps are left out
the count is three; adding one to it reports four

docs.explain: Column B holds three dates and two empty cells. COUNT would look for numbers, find none and answer 0, because these entries arrived as text rather than as dates. COUNTA answers a different question: how many cells hold something, anything. It returns 3. On a checklist the difference is the whole point. An empty cell means the step has not happened yet, so counting the filled ones is how you report progress. If a step gets a space typed into it, COUNTA counts that space as progress while COUNT still says 0. A progress bar that reads high sends you looking for stray spaces.

errors.text: The count was divided by zero, usually because the sharing formula ran on an empty progress column.
COUNTA was called with no argument at all. It needs at least one range or value to inspect.

docs.atWork: A launch checklist where the empty cells are the steps still to do, and the count of dated ones is what the status deck reports.
docs.outcome: Count filled cells, dates and labels included, so a checklist reports real progress.

seo.title: COUNTA in Excel: count non-empty cells
seo.description: Three dates and two blanks. COUNTA answers 3 because it counts anything filled, while COUNT answers 0 since these entries arrived as text.
